criteria.rule: High value: impact score at least 2.5 of 4 (halfway from "noticeably" to "substantially" moves the most important goal).
criteria.verdicts: high value = meets the rule · kept as a prerequisite = below the rule, but a high-value item cannot run without it · cut = below the rule and nothing high-value needs it · rejected on evidence = tried and measured worse or unidentified.

note: The scores are a model's judgment of the descriptions and evidence shown here; the verdict is the fixed rule applied to them.

items.title: A citable validation report
items.detail: One generated document with every comparison against published NASA data, when each criterion was written, the hits and the misses, the data-file digests and a version number, so an engineer can cite which estimates to trust and by how much.

evidence.line: Version 1.0 generated from the result files: 5 of 8 criteria met, the three misses listed; a test fails if the report does not match the current data.

items.title: Real aircraft only, each tied to its NASA report
items.detail: F-16, F/A-18 HARV, F-16XL-1 and F-106B: every dimension names the NASA table or figure it was read from; planforms are built from those numbers; anything traced from a drawing is labelled with its tolerance; no invented layouts.

evidence.line: F-106B's published area, chord and aspect ratio are reproduced from its triangle within 0.1%; the F-16's published area, span and mean chord exactly, with the sweep fitted to NASA's drawing (40.2° ± 2.5°); the F-16XL planform is 5% larger than the published wing area, and says so.

items.detail: One state for the share of vortex lift present, relaxing with a time constant of the order reported for delta wings; exact stepping; reduces to the static polar.

items.title: HARV rebuilt as a closed solid
items.detail: Monotone cubic curves through traced stations; every component a closed, oriented, welded 2-manifold; mesh checker tested on known and broken meshes.

evidence.line: Fuselage volume converges to the exact section integral; wing planform within 0.5% of the analytic trapezoid; outlines traced to ±0.3 ft, so no more accurate to the aircraft than its sources.
